questions: Is the input string A given without spaces (e.g., as a single contiguous line) or with spaces between characters as shown in the format description?
When counting the minimum number of elements to change, does changing an element mean flipping its bit (0↔1) or can it be set to any value (including the same value)?
Are we allowed to change any positions in A arbitrarily, or must the changes preserve some structure such as the grouping into triples?

If the majority value in a triple is tied (i.e., the three bits are 0,0,1 or 1,1,0), how is the majority defined—does the operation choose 0, choose 1, or is the input guaranteed never to contain such a tie?

Should the answer be the minimum number of bit flips needed to make A'_1 equal to the opposite of its original value, or to any value different from the original (including possibly the same value if the original majority is ambiguous)?
Are there any constraints on the time or memory limits that could affect the choice of algorithm for the maximum N=13?
Must the output be printed as an integer followed by a newline, or are other whitespace characters acceptable?
In the case where N=1 (string length 3), does the operation directly produce A'_1, and should the same rules for ties and changes apply as for larger N?
